steps.text: Here is a way to be sure. List the knight's eight possible jumps, then cross out the ones that do not work: a jump that would leave the board, and a jump onto one of its own pieces. A jump onto an enemy piece stays in, because that is a capture. The next board does exactly this for the knight you just met.

steps.caption: Eight candidates around d4. Only c2 is crossed out: a white pawn stands there. Four landing squares hold black pieces, and each is a capture, so they stay in.

line.say: Landing on a square with a black piece is a capture. Here the knight takes the bishop on e6.

claims.statement: The knight on d4 has exactly these seven landing squares.

steps.caption: At the start the knight on b1 has three candidates: a3, c3 and d2. The pawn on d2 is its own, so d2 is crossed out. The pawns directly in front of the knight change nothing.

line.say: The knight jumps over its own pawns and lands on c3, nearer the middle.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can go to exactly a3 and c3.

steps.caption: The bishop on c1 has no move yet: its own pawns on b2 and d2 block both diagonals. The knight beside it is free. Pieces between never block a knight; the landing square decides. Later you will meet pins, where a knight cannot move at all.

claims.statement: The bishop on c1 has no legal move at the start.
The knight on b1 has two legal moves.

steps.caption: Now the knight stands on c3, and Black has moved a knight too. Eight candidates: a2 and e2 hold white pawns and d1 holds the queen, so three are crossed out. Five jumps remain, one of them back to b1.

line.say: Jumping to e4 puts the knight in the centre of the board.

claims.statement: The knight on c3 has exactly five legal jumps.

steps.caption: The knight on d4 cannot jump to f5, because its own bishop stands there. But it defends that bishop. If the rook takes the bishop, the knight takes the rook back.

line.say: The knight takes the rook. A crossed-out square is still a square the knight defends.

claims.statement: One white piece, the knight, defends the bishop on f5.
One black piece, the rook, attacks the bishop on f5.
